questions.q: What does Paul always remember before God concerning the Thessalonians?
questions.a: Paul remembers their work of faith, their labor of love, and their patience of hope.

questions.q: In what four ways did the gospel come to the Thessalonians?
questions.a: The gospel came to the Thessalonians in word, in power, in the Holy Spirit, and in much assurance.

questions.q: What was happening to the Thessalonians as they received the word of the gospel?
questions.a: The Thessalonians received the word in much hardship.

questions.q: What was the Thessalonians’ attitude as they received the word of the gospel?
questions.a: The Thessalonians received the word with joy in the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: What happened to the word of the Lord after the Thessalonians received it?
questions.a: The word of the Lord rang out in every place their faith went out.

questions.q: What were the Thessalonians worshiping before they became believers in the true God?
questions.a: The Thessalonians were worshiping idols before they became believers in the true God.

questions.q: For what were Paul and the Thessalonians waiting?
questions.a: Paul and the Thessalonians were waiting for Jesus to come from heaven.

questions.q: From what does Jesus deliver us?
questions.a: Jesus delivers us from the wrath to come.

commentary.text: The faith, love, and patience of the Thessalonians, are evident tokens of their election which was manifested in the power with which the gospel came to them.
Its powerful and exemplary effects upon their hearts and lives.

Verses 1–5 As all good comes from God, so no good can be hoped for by sinners, but from God in Christ. And the best good may be expected from God, as our Father, for the sake of Christ. We should pray, not only for ourselves, but for others also; remembering them without ceasing. Wherever there is a true faith, it will work; it will affect both the heart and life. Faith works by love; it shows itself in love to God, and love to our neighbour. And wherever there is a well-grounded hope of eternal life, this will appear by the exercise of patience; and it is a sign of sincerity, when in all we do, we seek to approve ourselves to God. By this we may know our election, if we not only speak of the things of God with out lips, but feel their power in our hearts, mortifying our lusts, weaning us from the world, and raising us up to heavenly things. Unless the Spirit of God comes with the word of God, it will be to us a dead letter. Thus they entertained it by the power of the Holy Ghost. They were fully convinced of the truth of it, so as not to be shaken in mind by objections and doubts; and they were willing to leave all for Christ, and to venture their souls and everlasting condition upon the truth of the gospel revelation.

When careless, ignorant, and immoral persons are turned from their carnal pursuits and connexions, to believe in and obey the Lord Jesus, to live soberly, righteously, and godly, the matter speaks for itself. The believers under the Old Testament waited for the coming of the Messiah, and believers now wait for his second coming. He is yet to come. And God had raised him from the dead, which is a full assurance unto all men that he will come to judgment. He came to purchase salvation, and will, when he comes again, bring salvation with him, full and final deliverance from that wrath which is yet to come. Let all, without delay, flee from the wrath to come, and seek refuge in Christ and his salvation.
